text:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: Paging: p99 decode latency spike detected in prod-us-west-2 (models/redwood-open-7b v2). Alerting oncall.
Devin Tran: Seeing ~3x p99 and streaming stalls at tail for long sessions. p95 also creeping up. Repro on a few buckets of traffic, looks concentrated on decode path.
Lina Morales: Noted deploy 03:22 UTC included a new kernel selection heuristic and a compile flag tweak (`-O3 --fast-math`) on the shared decode image. Could be related.
Jorge Kim: Any correlation with recent TRT/flash attention updates? We rolled a TRT8+flash-attn kernel last night to the GPU pool.
Devin Tran: Yes, TRT8 was part of the 03:22 rollout. Metric slices where spikes happen align with machines that got the TRT8 image.
SRE Bot: Alert summary: 1901234567 - decode_p99_us-west-2 > 1.2s (baseline 0.35s). Streaming stalls: increase in incomplete stream sessions by 18% last 15m. Top error: CONTINUE_TIMEOUT on streaming shards.
Maria Chen: Customer impact: a handful of medium-tier customers reported timeouts on long streaming calls. No data plane errors; just retries and slow responses. CS already flagged 3 accounts.
Alexei Ivanov: Quick mitigation options: 1) Rollback TRT8/flash-attn kernel on affected pool. 2) Adjust routing to route traffic away from affected pool to older pool (fallback policy). 3) Temporarily disable the new compile flag via image rollback.
Lina Morales: I can cut a rollback image and patch the compile flags, but that takes ~15-20 min to build and push. Routing change should be fast.
Jorge Kim: I can put a dynamic route rule in front to divert 30-50% of traffic off the upgraded pool as a live mitigation. Do we want to fall back to redwood-open-7b v1 or to a quantized variant?
Devin Tran: Prefer falling back to v1 (same architecture) to minimize quality drift. Quantized variant may change outputs for customers.
SRE Bot: Action log: creating incident ticket INC-1901, priority P1, assigned to eng-oncall. Noting affected pools: usw2-gpu-pool-3 (TRT8), usw2-gpu-pool-4 (TRT8).
Maria Chen: Noting customer-facing message draft: "We're investigating intermittent latency for streaming responses in US-West; engineers are mitigating. No data loss. Apologies for the disruption." Will hold until we confirm mitigation.
Devin Tran: I'll apply the routing diversion now. Command I used (internal):
```
# divert 50% traffic away from pool-3
redwoodctl route update --region=us-west-2 --selector="pool=usw2-gpu-pool-3" --weight=0.5 --fallback-selector="pool=usw2-gpu-pool-2"
```
Lina Morales: After divert, monitor p99 and stream fail counts. I'll start a build of the rollback image and remove the `--fast-math` flag in the compile pipeline.
SRE Bot: Metric snapshot (pre-divert): decode_p99=1.28s, decode_p95=0.47s, streaming_incomplete=18%. Post-divert (2m): decode_p99=0.75s, streaming_incomplete=10%.
Jorge Kim: Good improvement. Recommend full rollback if build passes tests. If rollback will take >30m, continue diversion and start canary rollback to one node pool first.
Devin Tran: Initiating canary rollback on pool-3 node a1: `deployctl image rollback --pool=usw2-gpu-pool-3 --node=a1 --image=decode-runtime:v2024-11-14`.
Alexei Ivanov: FYI tests: run `./scripts/perf_check.sh --model redwood-open-7b --seq 2048` against canary after deploy. Watch p99 and stream throughput.
Lina Morales: Build finished and was validated on CI (perf regression < 2%). Pushing patch now, will flip canary.
SRE Bot: Deploy events: canary rollback started 1901236500, canary healthy at 1901236880. Metrics: canary decode_p99=0.36s, streaming stalls gone for canary traffic.
Maria Chen: Sending interim customer update now (appr. 1901237000): "We've diverted traffic and are rolling back a runtime change that impacted streaming latency. We're monitoring and will update soon."
Devin Tran: Canary looks solid. Kicking off gradual rollback to remaining nodes in pool-3 and pool-4. Expect full rollback in ~18 minutes.
Jorge Kim: After rollback completes, let's also revert the kernel selection heuristic change in the config repo and add a telemetry flag to capture kernel choices per request for next deploy.
Lina Morales: Agreed. I'll open PR with the revert + telemetry. Also adding a canary gate to block kernel selection changes without perf gate.
SRE Bot: Post-mitigation snapshot (1901238000): decode_p99=0.33s, decode_p95=0.34s, streaming_incomplete=1.2% — back to baseline.
Devin Tran: Great work. Logging post-incident tasks: root cause RCA (link to doc), add alert tuning to avoid noisy assemblies from compile flags, add rollback runbook steps for TRT rollouts.
Maria Chen: Customer follow-up: will reach out to affected accounts with summary and timeline after RCA drafted.
Jorge Kim: Handoff to next oncall @Lina Morales — I'll be available for questions but switching off in 30m.
Lina Morales: Taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and follow up on the PR and telemetry tasks. Marking incident resolved in the system once metrics stable for 30m.
SRE Bot: Incident INC-1901 moved to status: mitigated. Handoff recorded: Devin -> Lina. :white_check_mark:
Devin Tran: Thanks team :thumbsup:
